column1: # T390 -- AUTONOMOUS SCHEDULER MOVEMENT. A FOURTH BLIND SPOT, AND THE FIRST ROWS IN THIS FILE
# THAT NAME NO TASK, BECAUSE NO TASK DID IT.
# T388 accrued loan 8 through 15 April 2026 by API (EXECUTE PERIODICACCRUALACCOUNTING, tillDate
# 15 April 2026) and registered L28-L31 above. It stopped there. THE FINERACT SCHEDULER DID NOT.
# At 2026-08-28 16:01:00 UTC -- 00:01 on 2026-08-29 in Asia/Ulaanbaatar (+08), which is what the
# cron `0 1 0 1/1 * ? *` means -- job 11 "Add Accrual Transactions" ran and accrued the remaining
# THREE periods of loan 8, writing loan transactions 32/33/34 and journal entries 96-113, i.e.
# transactions L32/L33/L34. [job_run_history id 12721, start 16:01:00.049, end 16:01:00.12,
# status success; out/q4-job-run-history.txt.]
# WHY THIS BREAKS THE FILE'S MODEL, AND WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT IN T388.
# This file's obligation is "a task that fires a probe MUST append its rows in the same commit
# as its handoff". Here there IS NO TASK. The writer is app user 2 `system`
# [out/q7-who-is-user-2.txt] -- T388's own probes carry created_by 1 `mifos`. And the scheduler
# DOES NOT PASS THE COMMAND BUS: m_portfolio_command_source stops at 379, T388's last key, with
# no row for any of these eighteen legs [out/q2-command-source-tail.txt]. So the command-floor
# coverage argument written into oracle-state-baseline.sh -- "every API-driven write lands a
# command-source row" -- is TRUE AND IRRELEVANT to this movement. It is a fourth exception class
# beside T371's (a) consumed sequence, (b) direct SQL, (c) update below the floor:
#     (d) THE SCHEDULER. An in-process Spring Batch job writes journal entries with no
#         command-source row and no task to attribute them to. The ONLY reason this run went
#         red rather than silent is that job 11 writes to acc_gl_journal_entry, which IS one of
#         the two watched tables. A scheduled job touching any of the other 279 would be
#         invisible.
# IS IT BOUNDED? YES, FOR LOAN 8, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN HOPED. Loan 8 matured 2026-07-15 and
# has SIX schedule periods; six unreversed accrual transactions (29-34) now exist, the last dated
# 2026-07-15 [out/q6-business-date-and-schedule.txt]. There is nothing left on loan 8 to accrue,
# so tomorrow's 00:01 run adds nothing. m_business_date is EMPTY and the business-date config is
# off [out/q8-business-date-table.txt], so the job accrues to the system date and caught up in
# one sweep rather than dripping a period a day.
# WHAT IS *NOT* BOUNDED, AND IS THE REAL WARNING TO THE NEXT PROBER: job 11 is is_active = t and
# TASK THAT CREATES AN ACCRUAL-ACCOUNTING LOAN AND LEAVES IT PART-ACCRUED WILL HAVE THE
# SCHEDULER FINISH THE JOB FOR IT OVERNIGHT, and this file will go red on rows that task never
# fired. Register them here the same way, naming the job and the job_run_history id. Do NOT
# widen the floor, and do NOT teach the instrument to wave through anything written by user 2 --
# that would make every future scheduler write invisible, which is strictly worse than a red
# run somebody has to read.
# THESE ROWS USE THE `txn` TYPE UNCHANGED. Field 3 carries `SCHEDULER-JOB-11` where a task id
# would go. That is deliberate: the instrument's awk match is on field 2 and it prints field 3
# verbatim, so no code change is needed and the output says SCHEDULER-JOB-11 in the place a
# reader already looks for "who". Field 4 carries the fire that CAUSED it, not one that fired it.
# ---- fire 20260828-140005, AUTONOMOUS: scheduler job 11 completed T388's accrual series ----
